heading: EXT. SUSPENSION BRIDGE - INSPECTION GANTRY - DUSK

units.text: EXT. SUSPENSION BRIDGE - INSPECTION GANTRY - DUSK
Two hundred feet above a gray estuary.
The bridge's main cable rises in a long sweep, wrapped in galvanized wire.
A narrow steel gantry hangs beneath the deck on rails, rattling in the wind.
A woman and two men ride it, tethered to the rail by carabiners, as it creeps out along the span.
ASTRID MOLNAR (40s, structural engineer, yellow helmet, a hammer swinging from her belt) leads, tapping the cable with a small mallet.
She listens to each ring as a doctor listens to a chest.
DAMIAN OYELOWO (30s, rope-access tech, weathered, grinning) follows, checking every shackle with a gloved thumb.
His camera hangs at his hip, and he photographs every third bolt without being asked.
The third rides at the back: INSPECTOR LUDWIG VAHL (60s, state auditor, pressed overcoat under the harness, hat clamped under one arm).
He does not look down.
He does not look anywhere in particular.
Stop there.
units.name: ASTRID

units.text: Here?
units.name: DAMIAN

units.text: There. Eleven o'clock on the cable.
units.name: ASTRID

units.text: Damian leans out.
He points his lens.
The shutter clicks.
Fretting. Maybe a broken wire.
units.name: DAMIAN

units.text: How many?
units.name: ASTRID

units.text: I count four.
units.name: DAMIAN

units.text: Ludwig finally speaks, in a measured voice, as if reading from a script.
The report states the cables were replaced in 2019.
units.name: LUDWIG

units.text: They were wrapped in 2019.
units.name: ASTRID

units.text: Wrapped, replaced.
units.name: LUDWIG

units.text: Not the same.
units.name: ASTRID

units.text: He cleans his glasses with a handkerchief and looks, for the first time, at the cable.
He studies it for a long minute.
How long has she known?
units.name: LUDWIG

units.text: Who?
units.name: ASTRID

units.text: Whoever signed the report.
units.name: LUDWIG

units.text: Damian lowers his camera.
He looks at Astrid.
She looks at the water.
Since the day she signed it.
units.name: ASTRID

units.text: Ludwig puts his glasses back on.
The gantry shudders as a truck crosses the deck above, the whole structure humming like a plucked string.
Then I will need your name on the second report.
units.name: LUDWIG

units.text: I thought you'd never ask.
units.name: ASTRID

units.text: She holds out the mallet.
He takes it.
He taps the cable once, gently, and listens to the dull tone that rings back, the sound of something old and tired and honest.
Beyond them, a sodium lamp flickers on at the far tower, then the next, then the next, until the whole span is a string of pale lights floating over the dark water.
Is it going to hold?
units.name: DAMIAN

units.text: Tonight.
units.name: ASTRID

units.text: And tomorrow?
units.name: DAMIAN

units.text: She lays her palm flat against the cable, and does not answer.
The gantry creaks to a halt.
Ludwig glances at the straps looped around his waist, then at the two of them.
Slowly, he unhooks the carabiner from the rail and re-hooks it, twice, as a man might check a lock he already knows is secure.
Gentlemen. Madam. I am afraid of heights.
units.name: LUDWIG

units.text: We know.
units.name: DAMIAN

units.text: You did well.
units.name: ASTRID

units.text: He nods once.
They stand together on the thin steel, three small figures against an immense gray sky, until the wind drops enough for the gantry to turn back.
